# Task I - NAND-only and NOR-only gate counts

<!-- GENERATED by tools/verification/gate_count.py - do not edit by hand -->

Counts are obtained by **parsing the primitive instances** in [`rtl/arithmetic/nand_nor_arith.v`](../../rtl/arithmetic/nand_nor_arith.v) and evaluating the parsed netlist for every input vector against an independent integer-arithmetic reference. The Verilog modules themselves are also verified by simulation in `tb/task01/tb_half_full_adders.v`.

## Counting convention

* Only two-input NAND (or NOR) gates are allowed.
* An inverter is a two-input gate with both inputs tied together and **is counted as one gate** (column *tied-input inverters* shows how many of the total are inverters).
* A wire alias (e.g. `borrow = n2` in `half_subtractor_nor`) costs no gate.
* Logic depth = longest input-to-output path measured in gates.
* Counts describe the specific circuits in this repository. They are **not** claimed to be globally minimal; no exhaustive minimal-network search was performed.

## Results

| Circuit | NAND gates | NAND inverters | NAND depth | NOR gates | NOR inverters | NOR depth | Fewer gates |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Half adder | 5 | 1 | 3 | 6 | 1 | 5 | NAND |
| Half subtractor | 5 | 1 | 3 | 5 | 1 | 4 | tie |
| Full adder | 9 | 0 | 6 | 9 | 0 | 6 | tie |
| Full subtractor | 9 | 0 | 6 | 11 | 2 | 8 | NAND |

All eight parsed netlists matched the reference on every input vector (4, 4, 4, 4, 8, 8, 8, 8 vectors respectively).

## 4-bit ripple adders built from these cells

| Adder | Gates (4 x full adder) |
|---|---|
| `ripple_adder4_nand` | 4 x 9 = 36 two-input NAND |
| `ripple_adder4_nor`  | 4 x 9 = 36 two-input NOR |
| `ripple_adder4_gates` (xor/and/or) | 4 x (2 XOR + 2 AND + 1 OR) = 20 gates (mixed types, 2-input) |

## Justification (specific to the circuits above)

* **Shared sub-networks.** In every NAND design the first three gates (`n1 = nand(a,b)`, `n2 = nand(a,n1)`, `n3 = nand(b,n1)`) form the shared XOR front end; `n1` also yields the AND/carry term, so the carry costs one extra gate (an inverter) in the half adder and one gate in the full adder.
* **Half subtractor, NOR.** `n2 = nor(a, nor(a,b)) = ~a.b` is exactly the borrow, so the borrow output is free.
* **Why the full subtractor needs more NOR gates.** The borrow expression contains `~a.b`, and the NOR-based XOR produces XNOR first; recovering the XOR polarity for the second stage costs extra inverters (see the *NOR inverters* column).
* **Comparison.** For these constructions NAND is never worse than NOR and is strictly better for the half adder and full subtractor. Other realizations may exist; this report does not prove optimality.
